gorseller.istem: Close view of a vegetable garden in a Turkish Black Sea village: a weathered human hand has just lifted a flat grey stone, and underneath on dark damp soil lies a coiled slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard): smooth glossy bronze-copper skin made of tiny even flat scales that shine like polished metal, uniformly thick cylindrical body, small head merging into the body with no visible neck, short blunt rounded snout, small dark eyes with visible eyelids, no legs. Earthworm tunnels and roots in the soil, morning light.

A startled middle-aged village woman in a headscarf and work clothes stands in her vegetable garden, stepping back in fright and gripping a garden hoe, looking down at the ground; lettuce rows, a wooden fence, green hills behind. Expressive but not violent, nothing is being hit.

Detailed close-up portrait of the head and front body of a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard) resting on green moss: smooth glossy bronze-copper skin of tiny even flat scales shining like polished metal, small head merging into the body with no neck, short blunt rounded snout, small dark eye with a clearly visible lizard eyelid, tiny ear opening behind the eye, no legs. Soft dew drops on the moss.

Top-down view of a slow worm, a smooth glossy bronze-copper legless reptile shaped like a small polished snake, uniformly thick cylindrical body with absolutely no legs and no feet, tiny even flat scales, small blunt head that merges into the body with no neck, small dark eyes, its back grey-bronze and scattered with many small bright cobalt-blue spots, gliding across a mossy forest floor among fallen beech leaves, dappled sunlight.

Wide landscape of the Turkish Black Sea coast: steep lush green hills covered with beech and hazelnut trees, a small village with wooden houses and tea gardens on the slopes, a meadow and a country road in the foreground, the sea in the distance under soft clouds. No animals visible.

A forest clearing at the edge of a meadow in northern Turkey: a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard) with smooth glossy bronze-copper skin of tiny even scales, cylindrical body, small head with no neck, no legs, half hidden in leaf litter beside a mossy log and wild strawberries, ferns and morning mist.

Extreme macro close-up of the eye of a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard): the lower and upper eyelids are half closed in mid-blink, small dark round pupil, tiny smooth bronze scales around the eye, a small ear opening visible further back on the side of the head. Soft green blurred background.

Extreme macro close-up of the eye of a harmless grass snake (Natrix natrix): large round eye covered by a clear transparent spectacle scale, no eyelids, wide-open unblinking stare, keeled olive scales and the yellow collar patch behind the head. Soft green blurred background.

Garden scene in tall grass: on the left a blackbird looks curiously at a short separate piece of bronze tail lying on the bare soil; on the right, moving away into the grass, a slow worm, a smooth glossy bronze-copper legless reptile shaped like a small polished snake, uniformly thick cylindrical body with absolutely no legs and no feet, tiny even flat scales, small blunt head that merges into the body with no neck, small dark eyes, whose own tail now ends in a short blunt stump. Naturalist field-guide illustration.

In a wet vegetable garden after rain, a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard) with smooth glossy bronze-copper skin of tiny even scales, small head with no neck, no legs, is catching a small grey garden slug at the base of a lettuce plant that has slug holes in its leaves. Raindrops on the leaves, low morning light.

A small family vegetable garden in a Turkish Black Sea village just after a rain shower at dawn: rows of lettuce, tomato stakes, strawberry plants, a low dry stone wall, wooden house in the background, mist over green hills. Peaceful, no people.

On damp moss under a fern, an adult slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard) with smooth glossy bronze skin lies beside several newborn slow worms that are very thin, tiny and shiny, golden-silver on the back with a thin dark line along the spine and dark sides, each with a small head and no legs. Late summer light, tender mood.

Cross-section view of the ground in winter: snow on the surface with a few dry leaves and a stone, below it soil and tree roots, and in a small chamber underground several slow worms (legless lizards with smooth glossy bronze skin) curled up together hibernating. Cool blue and earthy brown tones, cosy and calm.

A suburban garden lawn in summer: a red push lawn mower parked on half-cut grass in the background; in the uncut grass in the foreground lies a slow worm, a smooth glossy bronze-copper legless reptile shaped like a small polished snake, uniformly thick cylindrical body with absolutely no legs and no feet, tiny even flat scales, small blunt head that merges into the body with no neck, small dark eyes, stretched out among the grass stems. Calm but with a subtle sense of danger, no harm shown.

Two careful human hands wearing garden gloves gently guide a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard) with smooth glossy bronze skin, small head, no legs, into a plastic bucket lying on its side, using a piece of cardboard, on a stone doorstep next to a garden. Kind, calm, respectful handling.

A nose-horned viper (Vipera ammodytes) coiled on a sunny mossy rock: thick heavy body, broad distinctly triangular head clearly wider than the thin neck, a small soft horn on the tip of the snout, vertical slit pupils, grey-brown body with a bold dark zigzag stripe down the back. Accurate field-guide illustration, calm snake seen from a respectful distance.

A young man crouches at a safe distance at the edge of a garden path and photographs with his mobile phone a small legless reptile lying in the grass a few metres away; he keeps his distance and does not touch it. Afternoon light, calm curious mood.

A wild corner of a garden at golden sunset: a pile of fallen leaves, a few flat stones, a rotting log, wildflowers and a low dry stone wall; from under a flat stone peeks the small blunt head and front of a slow worm, a smooth glossy bronze-copper legless reptile shaped like a small polished snake, uniformly thick cylindrical body with absolutely no legs and no feet, tiny even flat scales, small blunt head that merges into the body with no neck, small dark eyes. Warm, peaceful, hopeful.

Dramatic close-up of a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard) on the right side of the frame, its head raised slightly and looking toward the viewer: smooth glossy bronze-copper skin of tiny even scales shining like polished metal, small head merging into the body with no neck, short blunt snout, small dark eye with a clearly visible eyelid, no legs. Dark moss-green softly blurred background filling the left half of the image, plain and empty, strong rim light.

gorseller.istem: On damp moss under a fern, an adult slow worm lies in a loose curve. a slow worm (Anguis colchica, a legless lizard): smooth glossy bronze-copper skin made of tiny even flat scales that shine like polished metal, uniformly thick cylindrical body, small head that merges into the body with no visible neck, short blunt rounded snout, small dark eyes with visible lizard eyelids, no legs, not a snake. Beside it four newborn slow worms, each only about as long as a finger, pencil-thin, completely limbless like tiny shiny worms or pencil-thin snakes, with absolutely no legs, no feet, no toes, no claws anywhere on any animal, golden-silver on the back with one thin dark line along the spine and dark sides. Late summer light, tender mood.
